nb0cf30db050.s: Which of the following weakens the independence of a regulator?
o: Unrestricted removal at the discretion of the parent ministry
Removal only on grounds stated in the statute
nb0cf30db050.x: Unrestricted removal by the parent ministry weakens independence; fixed tenure, selection-committee appointment and statutory removal grounds are safeguards.

n9fde3a5e6c1.s: Regulatory capacity is regarded as part of State capacity because regulation is where the State meets the:
n9fde3a5e6c1.x: Regulation is one of the important points where the State meets the economy, so regulatory capacity is a component of State capacity.

n23513909ce6.s: Under the regulatory accountability framework, sanctions on regulated entities should be proportionate to:
n23513909ce6.x: The accountability framework calls for sanctions proportionate to intent, scale and harm, alongside parliamentary review, published orders and board oversight.

n070caad915a.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: TV Ratings Policy, 2026 – TRAI as sole regulator of rating agencies
DPDP Act – merged CCI with TRAI
CCI – penalised WhatsApp for abuse of dominance through data sharing
WhatsApp case – penalty imposed by the MIB
n070caad915a.x: The CCI penalised WhatsApp for abuse of dominance, while the DPDP Act separately restricts data cross-use; the TV Ratings Policy, 2026 made the MIB, not TRAI, the sole regulator.

n4a79aa7826c.s: India's oldest central trade union, the AITUC, co-founded by N.M. Joshi, was founded in:
n4a79aa7826c.x: AITUC was founded in 1920 with N.M. Joshi among its co-founders; 1947 is the year of INTUC.

ne38f9bc4155.s: The Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) is administered by the:
ne38f9bc4155.x: The MHA administers the FCRA; FEMA, 1999 is administered by the RBI and the Enforcement Directorate.

n54b87b1f1fe.s: Which of the following is a stated ground for cancellation of FCRA registration?
o: Having a registered office in a State other than New Delhi
Registration as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860
Receiving foreign funds in the designated FCRA account
n54b87b1f1fe.x: Non-functioning, breach of the Act or conditions and administrative defaults are grounds for cancellation; the location of the registered office is not.

nd40bfed6156.s: The Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS), affiliated with the RSS/BJP, was founded in:
nd40bfed6156.x: BMS was founded in 1955 and is associated with the RSS/BJP; 1947 is INTUC, 1948 HMS and 1920 AITUC.

n4d6217714eb.s: Pashu, Krishi, Bank, Bima and ____ Sakhi are community resource-person roles under DAY-NRLM.
n4d6217714eb.x: The listed DAY-NRLM roles are Pashu, Krishi, Bank, Bima and Poshan Sakhi; Nyaya Sakhi is not among them.

nfc8a671a904.s: Freedom of the press in India is read into which provision of the Constitution?
nfc8a671a904.x: Press freedom is part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

n48ace8ce895.s: The Press Council of India, which can warn, admonish or censure, has jurisdiction over:
n48ace8ce895.x: The PCI covers print media only and has no punitive powers.

n797cbd948db.s: The pressure-group technique of dealing with legislators and officials to promote or defeat legislation is called:
n797cbd948db.x: Lobbying means dealing with legislators and officials on legislation and regulation; propaganda shapes opinion and electioneering helps sympathetic candidates.

n7aa820bde0b.s: The blending of global and local cultural elements is known as:
n7aa820bde0b.x: Hybridisation is a blend of global and local elements; glocalisation is local adaptation, homogenisation is convergence to one pattern.

n0ebc100241d.s: Global integration in consumption and media is associated with:
o: Wider consumer choice and cultural fusion
Complete elimination of local cultural influences
n0ebc100241d.x: Global integration brings wider choice, global brands, media expansion and cultural fusion, but not the complete end of local culture.

n51141b9dfdd.s: Among the top international migration corridors, the India-UAE corridor ranks:
n51141b9dfdd.x: India-UAE ranks fifth and India-US sixth among the top migration corridors; India has the largest diaspora.

ne67386e7601.s: NITI Aayog (2022) projects the number of gig workers in India in 2029-30 at about:
ne67386e7601.x: Gig workers are projected to rise from 77 lakh (2020-21) to 2.35 crore by 2029-30, about 4.1% of the workforce.

n6107c3762d3.s: In the WTO era, farmer suicides linked to debt and crop failure were especially marked in:
n6107c3762d3.x: Debt-linked farmer suicides were especially marked in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh, while farmers also feared cheap imports under WTO rules.

nf227b8a4086.s: Which of the following farmer leaders supported globalisation?
nf227b8a4086.x: Sharad Joshi of the Shetkari Sanghatana supported globalisation; Nanjundaswamy and Tikait opposed the Dunkel Draft, GATT and WTO.

new.s: The AP Single Desk Portal promises all industrial clearances within:
new.x: Through a Single Desk Bureau, the AP Single Desk Portal gives all clearances within 21 working days.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Single Desk Portal for business clearances was launched in:
new.x: The AP Single Desk Portal was launched in April 2015 to simplify regulatory clearances.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about regulatory capacity:
1. TDSAT staff has been fixed at 52 posts since 2001.
2. About 67% of IBC cases exceed the 330-day limit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: TDSAT has 52 posts since 2001 and about 67% of IBC cases exceed the 330-day limit.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about regulatory capacity gaps in India?
o: Legal aid is available at only 9 of 23 Railway Claims Tribunal benches
The NGT has no IT division
India has a dedicated regulatory cadre
new.x: India has no dedicated regulatory cadre and relies on retired administrators, which is why a School for Regulations is proposed.

new.s: Because the DAE both promotes and regulates nuclear power, which Bill was proposed?
new.x: The DAE's dual role of promoter and regulator led to the proposed Nuclear Safety Regulatory Authority (NSRA) Bill.

new.s: After the SHANTI Act, 2025, commentators urged greater autonomy for which regulator to avoid regulatory capture?
new.x: After the SHANTI Act, 2025, more autonomy was urged for the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board to avoid capture.

new.s: Appeals against the orders of the PNGRB lie to:
new.x: APTEL hears appeals from CERC, SERCs and PNGRB.

new.s: Appeals against the orders of the Competition Commission of India lie to:
new.x: Since 26 May 2017, appeals against CCI orders go to NCLAT.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (appellate tribunal – orders appealed) is correctly matched?
new.x: TDSAT hears appeals from TRAI, IT Act officers and the Data Protection Board; CERC goes to APTEL, CCI to NCLAT and PFRDA to SAT.

new.s: The ordinance of 18 June 2010 that settled the SEBI-IRDA dispute placed ULIPs under:
new.x: The 2010 ordinance gave ULIPs to IRDA and set up a joint mechanism to resolve such disputes.

new.s: The joint mechanism set up in 2010 to resolve disputes between financial regulators was chaired by the:
new.x: The joint mechanism was chaired by the Finance Minister, with the RBI Governor as vice-chair.

new.s: The Regulatory Reform Bill, 2013, proposing a common framework for infrastructure regulators, was drafted by the:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
new.x: The Regulatory Reform Bill, 2013 was a Planning Commission draft for a common framework for infrastructure regulators.

new.s: The VBSA Bill, 2025 proposes one higher-education regulator replacing:
new.x: The VBSA Bill, 2025 proposes one regulator with three councils replacing the UGC, AICTE and NCTE.

new.s: Self-help groups in Andhra Pradesh are popularly called:
new.x: AP SHGs are popularly known as DWCRA groups, after Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas.

new.s: The Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP), which runs Velugu in AP, is:
o: An autonomous society of the Rural Development Department
new.x: SERP is an autonomous society of the Rural Development Department; Velugu was renamed Indira Kranthi Patham and later restored.

new.s: MEPMA, the urban SHG mission of Andhra Pradesh, was launched on:
new.x: MEPMA was created by G.O. Ms 414 of 4 June 2007 and launched on 1 September 2007.

new.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh is legally constituted as a:
o: Statutory body under an Act of Parliament
Society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860
new.x: RMK is a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, under the Ministry of WCD - not a company.

new.s: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was piloted by NABARD in:
new.x: NABARD (set up in 1982) piloted SHG-Bank Linkage in 1992; RMK came in 1993.

new.s: DAY-NRLM is implemented by the Ministry of:
new.x: DAY-NRLM is under the Ministry of Rural Development; RMK is under the Ministry of WCD.

new.s: Under the FCRA 2020 amendment, foreign contributions must first be received in a designated account at:
new.x: The 2020 amendment requires a designated FCRA account at SBI, New Delhi.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the FCRA 2020 amendment:
1. It banned sub-granting of foreign contributions.
2. It raised the ceiling on administrative expenses to 50 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: sub-granting was banned. Statement 2 is wrong: the cap was cut from 50 to 20 per cent.

new.s: The FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026 were notified on:
new.x: The Rules were notified on 22 June 2026; 25 March 2026 is when the Amendment Bill (later deferred) was introduced.

new.s: In India, public charitable trusts are registered under:
o: State laws such as the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950
new.x: Public charitable trusts come under State laws; the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 covers private trusts.

new.s: The National Policy on the Voluntary Sector, 2007 was brought out by the:
new.x: The 2007 policy was a Planning Commission document seeking an enabling environment and partnership with government.

new.s: The Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU), founded in 1970, is affiliated with the:
new.x: CITU (1970) is linked to CPI(M); AITUC to CPI, INTUC to Congress and HMS to the Socialists.

new.s: Which of the following is a peasant pressure group?
new.x: The Bharatiya Kisan Union is a peasant group; FICCI is business, IMA professional and HMS a trade union.

new.s: Which trade union has been keyed as the most powerful pressure group in India?
new.x: AITUC, India's oldest central trade union, was keyed as the most powerful pressure group (APPSC 2007).

new.s: The India Against Corruption movement (2011), led by Anna Hazare, led to the:
new.x: Anna Hazare's Jan Lokpal campaign led to the Lokpal Act, 2013; MKSS led to the RTI Act.

new.s: The Silent Valley movement is associated with:
new.x: Silent Valley is linked with Dr. Salim Ali, not Baba Amte, who was with the Narmada Bachao Andolan.

new.s: The Amaravati farmers' agitation against the three-capitals plan was led by the:
new.x: The agitation, from December 2019 to June 2024, was led by the Amaravati Parirakshana Samithi.

new.s: The Amaravati farmers' agitation, which began in December 2019, ended in June 2024 after:
new.x: It ended in June 2024 after 1,631 days, when the Naidu government took office.

new.s: The Press Council of India consists of a Chairman and:
new.x: The PCI has a Chairman and 28 members; the chairman is by custom a retired Supreme Court judge.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Press Council of India:
1. It was first set up in 1966 under the Press Council Act, 1965.
2. It now functions under the Press Council Act, 1978.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the PCI was first set up in 1966 under the 1965 Act and the present law is the Press Council Act, 1978.

new.s: In the RSF press freedom index (May 2026), India is placed in which category?
new.x: India is in RSF's 'very serious' category, reflecting problems such as paid news and concentrated ownership.

new.s: Filing PILs and court cases, as ADR did in electoral matters, is the pressure-group technique of:
new.x: Litigation means PILs and court cases; petitioning is written memoranda and lobbying is dealing with legislators.

new.s: According to Oxfam India's 'Survival of the Richest' (2023), the top 1% held what share of India's wealth in 2021?
new.x: Oxfam found the top 1% held 40.5% of wealth in 2021, while the bottom 50% held about 3%.

new.s: According to the World Inequality Report 2026, India's top 10% hold about what share of wealth?
new.x: The World Inequality Report 2026 puts India's top 10% at about 65% and the top 1% at about 40% of wealth.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Oxfam India's 'Survival of the Richest':
1. It was released in January 2023.
2. It found the bottom 50% held about 3% of India's wealth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the January 2023 report found the bottom 50% held about 3% of wealth.

new.s: 'Time-space distanciation' and the 'runaway world' are concepts of:
new.x: Giddens gave time-space distanciation and the 'runaway world'; Castells gave the network society.

new.s: Which thinker gave the concept of glocalisation and the 'world as a single place'?
new.x: Roland Robertson is linked with glocalisation; Ritzer with McDonaldisation.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the principles of McDonaldisation?
new.x: McDonaldisation rests on efficiency, calculability, predictability and control; diversity is not one of them.

new.s: India, the world's top remittance recipient, received about how much in remittances in 2024 (World Bank)?
new.x: India received about $129 billion in 2024, ahead of Mexico and China.

new.s: The World Migration Report, published every two years since 2000, is brought out by the:
new.x: The World Migration Report is a biennial publication of the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

new.s: APNRTS monitored about how many people from Andhra Pradesh in the Gulf (March 2026)?
new.x: APNRTS monitored about 10 lakh AP people in the Gulf; East and West Godavari and Kadapa are major emigration districts.

new.s: Joseph Stiglitz's 'Globalization and Its Discontents' (2002) mainly criticised the conditions imposed by the:
new.x: Stiglitz criticised IMF conditions in his 2002 book.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vandana Shiva – Globalization and Its Discontents
Seattle, 1999 – Protests against the WTO Ministerial
new.x: The 1999 Seattle protests targeted the WTO Ministerial; Navdanya is Vandana Shiva's, the 2002 book is Stiglitz's, and the first WSF was at Porto Alegre.

new.s: Vandana Shiva, a critic of biopiracy, is associated with:
new.x: Vandana Shiva founded Navdanya and campaigns for seed sovereignty; Shetkari Sanghatana was Sharad Joshi's pro-globalisation group.

new.s: Since 2017-18, the number of self-employed women in India has nearly:
new.x: Self-employed women have nearly tripled since 2017-18, not merely doubled.

new.s: About what share of India's coffee growers are small growers facing competition from Brazil and Vietnam?
new.x: About 98% of coffee growers are small and face competition from Brazil and Vietnam.

new.s: About what share of tertiary-educated youth were unemployed in India in 2023-24?
new.x: About 29% of tertiary-educated youth were unemployed in 2023-24.
